transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz (Redwood AE), Jonah Price (Redwood SE), Lina Kaur (Cardinal Legal), Tomás Rivera (Cardinal Head of Platform), Ayesha Khan (Cardinal Procurement)

Summary:
Quick intake to align procurement path from approval to production: MSA redlines, DPA expectations, SLA tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS options (BYOK vs Redwood-managed), pricing approval steps and pilot acceptance criteria. Action items and timeline were agreed.

Topics found:
- MSA exceptions and indemnity discussion
- Data residency and subprocessors in the DPA
- SLA targets and outage credits
- Pilot pricing and billing cadence
- KMS integration and audit log requirements

Transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: All right hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have the core folks from procurement and legal, thanks for making time. I have Jonah from our infra team here too for the technical bits.
[00:18] Tomás Rivera: Yeah thanks Samantha, we have a pretty tight window, finance wants to land something by end of the quarter, but legal will need to take a look at MSA/DPA. I'm Tomás, I run platform and i'll own the pilot.
[00:28] Ayesha Khan: Hi, Ayesha here, procurement. Key question for us is billing cadence and PO path; do you invoice monthly in arrears or is prepay required for Dedicated?
[00:36] Samantha Ortiz: Good question. For Hosted API we bill monthly in arrears by default, Dedicated we usually do a reserved commit that's invoiced monthly or quarterly depending on the contract, there is flexibility but it affects discounts. We'll send the pricing sheet.
[00:49] Lina Kaur: Lina, legal. We typically insist on a few MSA changes: limited indemnity, data return/return and deletion upon termination, and clear subprocessor lists for DPA. Also we need to confirm if you do BYOK with customer KMS or if keys are always Redwood-managed.
[01:06] Jonah Price: Hey Lina, on KMS we support both BYOK (customer-managed keys via our KMS integration) and Redwood-managed keys. The BYOK path will require a short onboarding for key rotation policies, and we'll provide HSM integration notes. There may be a small ops lead time for the private deployment.
[01:25] Tomás Rivera: When you say private deployment, do you mean VPC-hosted control plane or fully on-prem? We are leaning towards VPC with customer-managed KMS if possible.
[01:33] Jonah Price: VPC/private-cloud option is supported; full on-prem air-gapped is possible but longer lead time. For your use case VPC + BYOK is a common path.
[01:44] Ayesha Khan: From procurement we need SLA language: uptime target and credits. Our baseline request is 99.95 for production inference endpoints, is that something Redwood can commit to?
[01:55] Samantha Ortiz: We can discuss SLA tiers. For Hosted we can offer 99.9 standard, 99.95 for an enterprise tier usually tied to Dedicated or reserved capacity with the right monitoring hooks. The credit model is standard percentage-of-monthly-fee. We'll surface the SLA table in the MSA redline.
[02:11] Lina Kaur: Also need to confirm retention windows, audit logs, and ability to run customer-initiated audits or provide SOC 2 report.
[02:20] Samantha Ortiz: Yes we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and certificates, and we do support audit logs export. We'll add the list of artifacts and self-attestation docs.
[02:30] Speaker 1: there was a question earlier about subprocessors, we can provide a list but legal will want the right to object to new subprocessors or at least notification.
[02:40] Lina Kaur: Correct, and roll-forward: we may need a DPA clause that restricts cross-border transfers for this specific dataset given health data sensitivity.
[02:49] Jonah Price: Noted. Our DPA template has standard SCCs and we can map out data flow - we also support region pinning for inference to ensure residency. There might be export controls for some models, we'll flag that.
[03:06] Tomás Rivera: For the pilot, our acceptance criteria will be: end-to-end latency p95 under 250ms for 1k concurrent sessions, KV cache effectiveness > 30% for repeated context, and inference cost per token under our budget. Jonah, is that something you can benchmark?
[03:22] Jonah Price: Yes. We'll run a pilot harness with realistic prompt sets. I'll include KV cache measurement and sequence length distribution. For p95 we may need to tune batching and shards; we'll propose configs.
[03:33] Samantha Ortiz: And pricing for the 90-day pilot, we usually offer a reduced rate for pilot and waive overage for the first month if we agree on benchmarks. That helps procurement move faster.
[03:44] Ayesha Khan: Helpful. On billing terms, our preferred path is net30 after invoice; if pre-pay is required for a reserved commit we'll need to prepare a PO and finance signoff, which adds two weeks.
[03:56] Samantha Ortiz: Understood; we'll note both paths in next steps.
[04:01] Lina Kaur: A couple of MSA points that are likely to be redlined: 1) limitation of liability cap tie to fees, 2) termination for convenience notice period (we usually want 60 days), and 3) data return vs destruction language.
[04:13] Samantha Ortiz: We generally have a 30-60 day termination window depending on the contract size; liability caps can be negotiated for enterprise deals. We'll send a redline showing options.
[04:22] Tomás Rivera: On the tech side — can Redwood provide a temporary dedicated pool for the pilot so noisy neighbors don't skew latency? Or will we be on shared Hosted?
[04:32] Jonah Price: For pilot we can provision a small dedicated pool, it's a standard approach for enterprise benching. There's a small setup lead time (approx 3-5 business days) and a nominal charge for reserved capacity, but we can roll that into pilot pricing.
[04:46] Ayesha Khan: Procurement will need a price bind and an invoice template. Also, do you have an escrow or fallback if there are gross outages affecting production?
[04:55] Samantha Ortiz: We don't typically do escrow for software access, but we have contractual SLAs and escalation paths. We can discuss additional remedies in the commercial terms if necessary.
[05:06] Lina Kaur: One more: is there a subcontractor or subprocessors list for model hosting, e.g., cloud provider or any third-party inference partners? And do you have a process for notifying changes?
[05:17] Jonah Price: We use cloud providers in region; we maintain a subprocessors list and provide notifications with right-to-object windows per DPA. We'll include the current list.
[05:28] Speaker 2: Quick clarifying note — for data retention we can support configurable retention windows and we've got an option to zero-out KV caches on retention expiry.
[05:39] Tomás Rivera: Sounds good. For security, we want to be sure logs are tamper-evident; can audit logs be shipped to our SIEM?
[05:46] Jonah Price: Yes, we support log exports to S3 or push to your SIEM, and we can sign a SOC 2 addendum about integrity controls.
[05:57] Samantha Ortiz: Alright, let's walk through a high-level timeline: today 3/30 intake; by 4/2 we'll push MSA redline; by 4/5 Jonah will share pilot runbook; procurement to confirm PO timeline by 4/6; pilot to start week of 4/8 if approvals land.
[06:15] Ayesha Khan: That timeline is aggressive but feasible if legal moves quickly. I'll flag finance calendar and see if we can prep the PO draft.
[06:22] Lina Kaur: We'll need to loop in our privacy counsel for the DPA cross-border sections; I can do that once we see the redline.
[06:29] Tomás Rivera: One operational Q — how do you handle egress charges? If inference calls are in region, is there an extra transfer fee?
[06:36] Jonah Price: Egress is generally included in hosted pricing within region; cross-region transfers can incur additional charges. If we pin to a region there should be minimal egress. We'll call out egress assumptions in the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:50] Samantha Ortiz: Also note that certain model families may have separate licensing terms; we have a catalog and some models are third-party licensed which could change pricing. We'll note that in the model catalog link.
[07:02] Tomás Rivera: Ok thanks. For acceptance we'll need a short sign-off form: baseline SLA met, latency p95 met, and cost not exceeded by more than 15% of the pilot quote.
[07:12] Samantha Ortiz: We'll produce that acceptance template.
[07:15] Ayesha Khan: Are there any export control or ITAR considerations? We're healthcare but not necessarily defense, but we do have partners in EMEA and APAC.
[07:24] Jonah Price: We'll run the compliance checklist; some models and regions have export controls. We'll flag any restrictions.
[07:32] Lina Kaur: When you send the MSA redline please include an explanation of any proposed changes so our counsel can triage quickly.
[07:39] Samantha Ortiz: Absolutely. We'll include a redline + negotiation memo.
[07:42] Speaker 1: There's also the question of support entitlements and escalation deadbands — do you offer 24/7 PagerDuty on enterprise?
[07:50] Samantha Ortiz: Yes, enterprise support includes 24/7 on-call and a named technical account manager for the duration of the contract. We'll list the support tiers.
[07:58] Tomás Rivera: Great. One last thing — data residency: we need assurance that backup snapshots won't be replicated across borders for this tenant. That's non-negotiable for the compliance team.
[08:10] Jonah Price: We'll mark your tenant and ensure snapshots are region-scoped. We'll document the backup policy and options in the security pack.
[08:20] Ayesha Khan: Cool. From procurement side please put the pilot pricing as a separate line item so we can approve it quickly without committing to a longer reserved capacity.
[08:30] Samantha Ortiz: Noted. We'll separate pilot cost and reserved commitment costs.
[08:34] Lina Kaur: We'll review redline and get back with a consolidated list of exceptions. Can Redwood accept a two-week standstill for material DPA changes while we route internally?
[08:44] Samantha Ortiz: We can be flexible on review windows; we'll note a 10 business day review window in the negotiation memo.
[08:50] Tomás Rivera: Alright let's recap next steps.
[08:54] Samantha Ortiz: Recap: 1) Redwood sends MSA redline + DPA summary by 2026-04-02; 2) Jonah sends pilot runbook and benchmark checklist by 2026-04-05; 3) procurement confirms PO/finance timeline by 2026-04-06; 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-04-08. Action items captured.
[09:13] Ayesha Khan: That works. Thanks everyone.
[09:16] Lina Kaur: Thanks. We'll loop privacy counsel after the redline.
[09:20] Jonah Price: Thanks all, I'll get the runbook started, expect a draft by Monday.
[09:24] Samantha Ortiz: Thanks team, we'll follow up in email with attachments: MSA redline, DPA pack, pricing grid, and pilot checklist.
[09:30] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional misattribution and minor ASR errors around technical terms (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), some names may be slightly misspelled.

Links referenced during call (to be attached in follow up):
